user_request_examples: Create a robot on a moving base that can stack blocks
Set up a mobile manipulator to transfer objects between tables
Build a robot that extends its workspace with linear motion
Make a robot with a sliding base pick and stack cubes
scenario_description: A Franka Panda arm mounted on a 1-DOF prismatic base moves between two tables (2.4m apart) to pick blocks from the right table and stack them on the left table. This demonstrates coordinated base-arm motion planning and extended workspace manipulation.

mobile_base.reason: Extends robot workspace beyond fixed-base reach

robot_arm.mounting: Fixed to arm_mount on top of mobile base

kinematic_chain.structure: world → world_link → mobile_base → arm_mount → panda_link0 → ... → panda_hand
kinematic_chain.reason: Virtual link allows base joint to be part of robot model

complexity_factors.mobile_base_modeling: Requires virtual link for kinematic chain
complexity_factors.coordinated_planning: Must plan base and arm motion together
complexity_factors.workspace_analysis: Two distinct workspace regions connected by base motion

step1_mobile_base_setup.description: Create mobile base with 1-DOF prismatic joint
key_points: Virtual world_link with negligible mass (0.001 kg)
Prismatic joint along X-axis with ±1.5m limits
Arm mount platform fixed on top of base
Weld world_link to actual world frame

step2_arm_attachment.description: Mount Panda arm on mobile base
step2_arm_attachment.method: Fixed joint from arm_mount to panda_link0

strategy_1_sequential.description: Move base first, then manipulate with arm
steps: IK to pick block with arm only
IK to place/stack with arm only
strategy_1_sequential.cons: Not optimal, two base motions per block

steps: Plan transit configuration while moving base

sequence: Pick red block from right table
Place red block on left table
Place green block on top of red block
Place blue block on top of stack

virtual_link_pattern.reason: Drake requires all joints to connect two bodies

expected_behavior.initialization: Base at center (x=0), arm at home
expected_behavior.phase_1: Base moves to right (x=0.8), arm picks red block
expected_behavior.phase_2: Base transits to left (x=-0.8) with block
expected_behavior.phase_3: Arm places red block on left table
expected_behavior.repeat: Same for green and blue blocks with increasing stack height
expected_behavior.completion: All three blocks stacked on left table, base returns to center

validation_criteria.efficiency: Uses base motion optimally (no unnecessary travels)

solutions: Fix base position first, solve 7-DOF IK for arm
Use sequential optimization: base position then arm config
Provide good initial guess close to solution

base_arm_collision.symptom: Arm collides with mobile base during motion
solutions: Add collision geometry to base and arm mount
Add collision avoidance constraints to planner
Keep arm in safe configuration during base motion
Add stabilization wait time after placement

extensions.3dof_planar_base: Add Y motion and rotation for full planar mobility
extensions.dual_arm_mobile: Two arms on mobile base for bimanual tasks

learning_outcomes.mobile_base_modeling: How to add prismatic bases to manipulators
learning_outcomes.virtual_links: Using zero-mass links for kinematic closure
learning_outcomes.high_dof_ik: Solving IK for combined base-arm systems

code_snippets.create_virtual_link: world_link with mass=0.001 for kinematic chain
code_snippets.10dof_ik: ik = InverseKinematics(plant, context)  # Includes base joint
